answer.text: Two molecules of the three carbon acid 3-PGA
answer.line: Five carbons plus one makes six, and that six-carbon piece splits at once into two 3-PGA.

steps: Count carbons. RuBP brings 5 and carbon dioxide brings 1, so RuBisCO makes a 6-carbon piece.
That 6-carbon piece is unstable. It splits at once into two 3-carbon acids, 3-PGA.
G3P comes later, after ATP and NADPH reduce 3-PGA. Stop at the first step, as the stem does.

choices.text: One two carbon fragment and one three carbon acid
choices.note: That pair comes from RuBisCO adding O2 instead of CO2: photorespiration. With carbon dioxide you get two 3-PGA.

choices.text: Two molecules of G3P, ready to leave the cycle
choices.note: G3P appears after ATP and NADPH reduce 3-PGA. It is not what comes out of the first step.

choices.text: Two molecules of the three carbon acid 3-PGA
One stable six carbon sugar that leaves the cycle
choices.note: A 6-carbon piece does form, but it lasts an instant. It splits in half before anything leaves the cycle.
Oxaloacetate is what PEP carboxylase makes in C4 and CAM plants. RuBisCO makes 3-PGA.

legend.label: Fixation by RuBisCO: RuBP and CO2, 5 + 1 = 6 carbons, split at once into two 3-PGA
Reduction: ATP and NADPH turn 3-PGA into G3P
Regeneration: ATP rebuilds RuBP from G3P

visual.alt: The Calvin cycle as boxes and arrows. RuBP, 5 carbons, and CO2, 1 carbon, join into a 6-carbon piece that splits at once into two 3-PGA of 3 carbons each, outlined as the answer. Arrows then run on to G3P, using ATP and NADPH, and back to RuBP.
visual.caption: Add the carbons along the green arrows: 5 plus 1 is 6. Then watch the 6 break into two 3s.
